newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Moody's rates SEOULBANK sub-debt Baa3.
newsitem.headline: Moody's rates SEOULBANK sub-debt Baa3.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service on Friday said it had assigned a rating of Baa3 to South Korea's SEOULBANK for its issue of subordinated floating rate notes, due 2006.
This is the first time that Moody's has rated SEOULBANK's subordinated debt, it said in a statement.
"The rating reflects SEOULBANK's position as a major South Korean financial institution in a supportive regulatory environment, as well as its low profitability and poor asset quality," Moody's said.
SEOULBANK's long-term senior debt and deposits are currently rated Baa2, its short-term deposits and euro-commercial paper Prime-2, and its bank financial strength rating is E+.

Moody's said the bank's asset quality was weak due to its large portfolio of policy loans. The slowdown in the South Korean economy was also pressuring loan quality as bankruptcies among small and mid-sized firms rose sharply.

SEOULBANK suffered from low core profitability and the bank reported very low net earnings for 1995 and a loss for the first half of 1996. This was linked to large provisions for loan losses and the a decline in the value of its investment portfolio, Moody's said.
In 1995, SEOULBANK reported net profit of five billion won against 53.1 billion a year earlier.

"Profitability is likely to be poor for some time as the bank makes the necessary loan loss provisions and charge-offs, as well as rationalise its cost structure," Moody's said. "Korea's ongoing deregulation of the financial service industry has introduced new competitive forces and will pressure margins," it said.
